title: Job Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Job chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Job Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Job Chapter 22.

questions.question: In Job 22, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty?
Thou hast not given water to the weary
For thou hast taken a pledge from thy brother
questions.explanation: This appears first in the chapter as stated in Job 22:1.

questions.question: According to Job 22, can a man be profitable unto God?
questions.explanation: Job 22:2 poses the question of profitability, implying that a man cannot be profitable to God.

questions.question: What question does Eliphaz ask regarding the Almighty's pleasure in righteousness?
options: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty?
questions.explanation: Job 22:3 asks if it is any pleasure to God that a man is righteous or if it is gain to Him.

questions.question: Will God reprove Job for fear of him?
questions.explanation: Job 22:4 indicates that God will not reprove Job for fear of him.

questions.question: What does Eliphaz say about Job's wickedness?
questions.explanation: Job 22:5 states that Job's wickedness is great and his iniquities are infinite.

questions.question: What did Job take from his brother, according to Eliphaz?
questions.explanation: Job 22:6 mentions that Job took a pledge from his brother for nought.

questions.question: According to Eliphaz, what has Job withheld from the hungry?
questions.explanation: Job 22:7 states that Job has withheld bread from the hungry.

questions.question: Who had the earth according to Eliphaz?
questions.explanation: Job 22:8 says that the mighty man had the earth.

questions.question: What has Job done to widows, according to Eliphaz?
questions.explanation: Job 22:9 states that Job has sent widows away empty.

questions.question: What surrounds Job, as stated by Eliphaz?
questions.explanation: Job 22:10 mentions that snares are round about Job.

questions.question: Does Eliphaz claim that Job's iniquities are infinite?
questions.explanation: Job 22:5 states that Job's iniquities are infinite.

questions.question: Is it true that Job has stripped the naked of their clothing?
questions.explanation: Job 22:6 states that Job has stripped the naked of their clothing.

questions.question: Is it true that Eliphaz is the first speaker in Job 22?
questions.explanation: Job 22:1 shows that Eliphaz the Temanite answered first.

questions.question: Is it false that Job provided plenty of food for the hungry?
questions.explanation: Job 22:7 indicates that Job has withheld bread from the hungry.

questions.question: Is it false that Job has taken a loan from his brother?
questions.explanation: Job 22:6 states that Job took a pledge from his brother for nought, not a loan.

medium.title: Job Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Job Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Job 22:12 indicate about God's presence?
options: God is in the height of heaven
God is limited by the clouds
God does not watch over the stars
questions.correctAnswer: God is in the height of heaven
questions.explanation: This is correct because Job 22:12 states, 'Is not God in the height of heaven?' indicating His omnipresence and majesty.

questions.question: What does Job 22:19 promise will happen if someone is righteous, as mentioned in Job 22:18?
options: They will see their substance cut down
They will be filled with good things
They will suffer like the wicked
questions.explanation: Job 22:19 states, 'The righteous see it, and are glad,' which directly follows the promise of God filling the houses of the wicked with good things in Job 22:18.

questions.question: What does Job 22:11 say about darkness?
questions.explanation: Job 22:11 states, 'Or darkness, that thou canst not see,' indicating that darkness hides understanding and perception.

questions.question: According to Job 22:14, how does God perceive the world?
options: He walks in the circuit of heaven
He is unaware of earthly affairs
He is limited by human actions
questions.correctAnswer: He walks in the circuit of heaven
questions.explanation: Job 22:14 mentions that God 'walketh in the circuit of heaven,' illustrating His sovereignty and awareness of all things.

questions.question: What does Job 22:16 describe about wicked men?
options: They were cut down out of time
They live long and fruitful lives
questions.correctAnswer: They were cut down out of time
questions.explanation: Job 22:16 states that the wicked men 'were cut down out of time,' indicating their sudden downfall due to their actions.

questions.question: According to Job 22:18, what is said about the counsel of the wicked?
options: It is filled with good things
questions.explanation: Job 22:18 states, 'but the counsel of the wicked is far from me,' indicating God's disapproval of wickedness.

questions.question: What does Job 22:13 question about God?
options: How can He judge through the dark cloud?
How does He create the stars?
How does He provide for the righteous?
How does He know the hearts of men?
questions.correctAnswer: How can He judge through the dark cloud?
questions.explanation: Job 22:13 states, 'And thou sayest, How doth God know? can he judge through the dark cloud?' expressing doubt about God's omniscience.

questions.question: In Job 22:20, what is said about the substance of the righteous?
questions.explanation: Job 22:20 states, 'Whereas our substance is not cut down,' indicating the stability of the righteous compared to the wicked.

questions.question: According to Job 22:4, why might God reprove a man?
questions.explanation: Job 22:4 states, 'Will he reprove thee for fear of thee?' suggesting that God does not act out of fear of man.

questions.question: What does Job 22:5 imply about Job's actions?
options: He is favored by the Almighty
questions.explanation: Job 22:5 states, 'Is not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite?' indicating a serious accusation against Job.

questions.question: What does Job 22:9 reveal about Job's treatment of the needy?
questions.explanation: Job 22:9 states, 'Thou hast sent widows away empty,' which reflects a failure to care for the vulnerable.

questions.question: In Job 22:10, what is said about Job's situation?
options: He is in a state of peace
questions.explanation: Job 22:10 states, 'Therefore snares are round about thee,' indicating trouble and entrapment.

questions.question: Is it true that God can judge through the dark cloud?
questions.explanation: This is false because Job 22:13 questions God's ability to judge through the dark cloud, implying He can see beyond it.

questions.question: Is it true that God filled the houses of the wicked with good things?
questions.explanation: This is true as Job 22:18 states, 'Yet he filled their houses with good things,' indicating God's provision even for the wicked.

questions.question: Is it true that the righteous will suffer like the wicked according to Job 22:19?
questions.explanation: This is false because Job 22:19 indicates that 'the righteous see it, and are glad,' contrasting their fate with that of the wicked.

hard.title: Job Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Job Chapter 22.

questions.question: According to Job 22:21, what is the result of acquainting yourself with God?
questions.explanation: Job 22:21 states, 'Acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace: thereby good shall come unto thee.' The direct result mentioned is that good will come to the person who acquaints themselves with God.

questions.question: What does Eliphaz urge Job to receive from God's mouth in Job 22:22?
questions.explanation: Job 22:22 says, 'Receive, I pray thee, the law from his mouth, and lay up his words in thine heart.' The emphasis is on receiving the law directly from God’s mouth.

questions.question: In Job 22:23, what is promised if Job returns to the Almighty?
questions.explanation: Job 22:23 states, 'If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up, thou shalt put away iniquity far from thy tabernacles.' The promise is restoration and being built up upon returning to God.

questions.question: What metaphor is used in Job 22:24 to describe accumulating wealth?
questions.explanation: Job 22:24 says, 'Then shalt thou lay up gold as dust, and the gold of Ophir as the stones of the brooks.' The metaphor compares gold to dust to emphasize abundance.

questions.question: According to Job 22:25, what will the Almighty be to Job?
questions.explanation: Job 22:25 says, 'Yea, the Almighty shall be thy defence, and thou shalt have plenty of silver.' God is described as a defense, a protector.

questions.question: What will happen when Job makes his prayer to God according to Job 22:27?
questions.explanation: Job 22:27 states, 'Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he shall hear thee, and thou shalt pay thy vows.' The verse promises that God will hear the prayers.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'shuv' (שוב) in Job 22:23 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'shuv' (שוב) in Job 22:23 means 'return' or 'turn back,' indicating repentance or returning to God as stated in the verse.

questions.question: Which literary device is most prominent in Job 22:21-30?
questions.explanation: The passage Job 22:21-30 employs parallelism, a common Hebrew poetry technique where ideas are balanced and repeated in different forms to reinforce the message.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of divine defense and deliverance found in Job 22:25?
questions.explanation: Psalm 18:2 describes God as a rock, fortress, and deliverer, paralleling Job 22:25 where the Almighty is called 'thy defence.'

questions.question: Which Old Testament book contains a similar exhortation to 'lay up his words in thine heart' as in Job 22:22?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:6 exhorts the people to keep God's commandments in their heart, similar to Job 22:22's urging to 'lay up his words in thine heart.'

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Job 22:21?
questions.explanation: Job 22:20 directly precedes verse 21; it discusses the remnant of the wicked being consumed by fire before Eliphaz urges Job to acquaint himself with God in verse 21.

questions.question: How does the concept of 'putting away iniquity' in Job 22:23 relate to New Testament teachings?
options: It parallels repentance and forgiveness found in Acts 3:19
It contradicts the New Testament emphasis on grace
It is unrelated to New Testament doctrines
questions.correctAnswer: It parallels repentance and forgiveness found in Acts 3:19
questions.explanation: Job 22:23's call to 'put away iniquity' aligns with Acts 3:19, which calls for repentance and turning to God for forgiveness, showing continuity in divine expectations.

questions.question: What type of literary structure is illustrated by the thematic progression in Job 22:21-30, moving from spiritual reconciliation to material blessings?
questions.explanation: The passage shows progressive parallelism, where each verse builds on the previous one, moving from reconciliation with God to tangible blessings, a known Hebrew poetic structure.

questions.question: Does Job 22:29 suggest that God will save the humble person?
questions.explanation: Job 22:29 states, 'and he shall save the humble person,' directly affirming that God saves the humble.

questions.question: Is it true that Job 22:5 says 'Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous?'?
questions.explanation: Job 22:5 actually says, 'Is not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite?' The question about God's pleasure in righteousness is in Job 22:3, not 22:5.

theological.title: Job Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Job Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 22:3 teach about the nature of righteousness before God?
options: God takes pleasure in human perfection
Human righteousness does not profit God
God judges strictly based on human righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Human righteousness does not profit God
questions.explanation: Job 22:3 questions whether it is any pleasure or gain to God that a man is righteous or makes his ways perfect, implying that human righteousness does not profit God.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning divine judgment is taught in Job 22:4?
options: God reproves out of fear of man
God enters judgment with the wicked
God’s judgment is not motivated by fear of man
Man’s righteousness compels God to judge
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is not motivated by fear of man
questions.explanation: Job 22:4 asks if God will reprove or enter judgment because He fears man, teaching that God's judgment is not motivated by fear of man.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 22:5 affirm about human sinfulness?
options: Human sinfulness is limited and finite
Human sinfulness is great and infinite
Sin is a temporary condition easily removed
questions.correctAnswer: Human sinfulness is great and infinite
questions.explanation: Job 22:5 states that wickedness is great and iniquities are infinite, affirming the doctrine of the extensive and deep corruption of human sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Job 22:12 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Job 22:12 points to God being in the height of heaven and the stars being very high, demonstrating God’s transcendence above creation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Job 22:27?
questions.explanation: Job 22:27 teaches that when one makes prayer unto God, He shall hear, emphasizing God’s attribute as the hearer of prayer.

questions.question: How does the warning in Job 22:16 about the flood that destroyed the wicked connect to broader biblical themes?
options: It parallels the judgment of the flood in Genesis as a warning of divine justice
It suggests floods are a symbol of blessing
It denies the possibility of divine judgment
It teaches that all disasters are natural, not divine
questions.correctAnswer: It parallels the judgment of the flood in Genesis as a warning of divine justice
questions.explanation: Job 22:16 references a flood that overthrew wicked foundations, connecting to Genesis flood narratives symbolizing God's judgment on sin.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is prepared for by Job 22:21's exhortation to 'Acquaint now thyself with him'?
options: The call to faith and peace with God anticipates New Testament salvation
The establishment of a new law covenant
questions.correctAnswer: The call to faith and peace with God anticipates New Testament salvation
questions.explanation: Job 22:21’s command to acquaint oneself with God and be at peace foreshadows the salvific relationship with God revealed fully in the New Testament.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 22:23 and Job 22:24 teach about sanctification and divine blessing?
options: Turning to God leads to both moral renewal and material blessing
Divine blessing is unrelated to moral behavior
Iniquity is preserved even after repentance
questions.correctAnswer: Turning to God leads to both moral renewal and material blessing
questions.explanation: Job 22:23 speaks of putting away iniquity after returning to God, and 22:24 promises abundance of gold, combining sanctification and divine blessing.

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine justice and human response is found in Job 22:15 and Job 22:17?
options: Wicked men reject God’s presence yet experience His judgment
The wicked are justified by their denial of God
God rewards the wicked for their denial
questions.correctAnswer: Wicked men reject God’s presence yet experience His judgment
questions.explanation: Job 22:15 notes wicked men’s way, and 22:17 records their rebellion against God, indicating their rejection yet they face consequences.

questions.question: What theological synthesis do Job 22:28 and Job 22:29 provide regarding divine providence and humility?
options: Divine providence establishes decrees and lifts up the humble
Divine providence is arbitrary and favors the proud
The humble are overlooked by God
questions.correctAnswer: Divine providence establishes decrees and lifts up the humble
questions.explanation: Job 22:28 speaks of decrees being established, and 22:29 shows God’s salvation for the humble, linking providence and humility.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Job 22:5–10 accuses Job unfairly of great wickedness without cause. What does this passage actually teach about divine justice and human sin?
options: It asserts that sin has social consequences and invites divine judgment
It excuses Job’s suffering as random
It emphasizes God’s indifference to sin
questions.correctAnswer: It asserts that sin has social consequences and invites divine judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 5–10 accuse specific social sins and describe snares and fear as consequences, teaching that sin prompts divine judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about the efficacy of prayer is taught in Job 22:27 and Job 22:28?
options: Prayer is efficacious and divine response is assured
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer is efficacious and divine response is assured
questions.explanation: Job 22:27 affirms God hears prayers, and 22:28 states decrees will be established, teaching prayer’s efficacy.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Job 22:30 regarding God's defense of the innocent?
questions.explanation: Job 22:30 states God delivers the innocent by the pureness of their hands, emphasizing His attribute of justice.

questions.question: What theological insight about divine hiddenness and knowledge is found in Job 22:13–14?
options: God’s knowledge is not hindered by darkness or clouds
God cannot see through thick clouds
God’s knowledge is limited to the visible
God is unaware of human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God’s knowledge is not hindered by darkness or clouds
questions.explanation: Verses 13–14 describe clouds as covering but God still sees and walks in heaven’s circuit, affirming His omniscience despite hiddenness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine protection and human security does Job 22:25 and Job 22:26 teach?
options: Divine protection leads to blessings and joy in God
Blessings depend solely on human effort
Security is found in material wealth alone
questions.correctAnswer: Divine protection leads to blessings and joy in God
questions.explanation: Job 22:25 speaks of the Almighty as defense with plenty of silver, and 22:26 about delighting in God, linking protection and joy.
